persona: Apparel art director for independent labels

designs.title: Byron Bay
designs.why: The Cape Byron lighthouse makes this one specific to the place rather than a stock beach. The engraving is crisp at full size and holds as a single ink on both tees. The 'Good Vibes' and 'Ocean People Freedom' filler lines feel generic, and there's a break in the outer ring at 3 o'clock that reads as a defect, not distressing.
designs.fix: Close the gap in the outer ring and swap the filler taglines for one local detail, like the coordinates or 'Cape Byron'.

designs.title: Playa Venao
designs.why: It's competent and clean in one ink, but the scene could be any beach: stock palm, signpost, wave. Stacking the 'Pacific Vibes' block next to a SURF/EXPLORE/RELAX/REPEAT sign piles on cliché and fights the clarity of the badge.
designs.fix: Drop the motivational signpost and put in one recognisable Venao feature, like the horseshoe bay and headland, so it earns its $50.

designs.title: Ericeira
designs.why: This is the strongest of the set. The clifftop whitewash town, stone stairs and leaning board are unmistakably Portugal, and the engraving texture really pays off up close. 'Small Town Big Waves' is the one tagline here with some wit. It works on the white main tee and also carries on black.
designs.fix: Repair the break in the outer ring at the right edge. Ericeira is a World Surfing Reserve, which is a nice optional nod.

designs.title: San Juan del Sur
designs.why: The long name is jammed into the arc: 'SUR' crowds the ring and the palm crown collides with the lettering. 'Pura Vida' is Costa Rica's slogan, not Nicaragua's, and a TACOS sign reads Mexican. Locals and well-travelled customers will notice, and that undermines a place shirt.
designs.fix: Make 'San Juan del Sur' smaller with more tracking so it clears the ring. Replace 'Pura Vida' and 'Tacos' with Nicaraguan references (for example 'Nica' or the Cristo de la Misericordia, which is already drawn).

designs.title: Haleiwa
designs.why: The North Shore ridgeline and the shave-ice sign ground it in the real place, and the letter-spaced HALEIWA arc is the cleanest wordmark in the series. It sits well on the black main tee. There's still more tagline text than it needs: 3 lines at the top plus 4 at the side.
designs.fix: Cut the 4-line 'Good Waves Kind People' side block so the scene and wordmark have room, and close the ring break.

designs.title: Puerto Escondido
designs.why: The Mexican Pipeline barrel is right for the spot and the wave is the best-rendered one in the set. But the title arc runs far down the left side and touches the ring, and there's a stray cloud with a vertical squiggle near the sun that reads as an artefact up close. The taglines are generic.
designs.fix: Tighten the title so it sits within the top arc like the others, and clean up the stray cloud mark beside the sun.

designs.title: Montañita
designs.why: The palapa bar and signposts (Surf/Food/Music/Friends) suit Montañita's party-town character, and the Ñ is handled properly. But the left third is very dense: hut, sign, palms and a 4-line text block all fighting, so at 3 m it turns into a dark mass on the black tee.
designs.fix: Remove the 'Good Waves Better People' side text and thin the foliage behind the hut so the left side breathes.

designs.title: Tamarindo
designs.why: It's the most generic of the eight: palm, wave and sun with nothing that says Tamarindo. 'Pura Vida Siempre' is at least correct for Costa Rica. The execution is clean, but at $50 a template beach with a name swapped in won't hold up next to independent-label product.
designs.fix: Add one local signifier, such as the estuary mouth, Isla Capitán or a leatherback turtle, in place of a duplicated palm.
